Motivation
The consumer read path avoids a per-record copy for the record value.KIP-863added aByteBuffermethod toDeserializerso thatCompletedFetch#parseRecordcan hand the deserializerthe record value straight from the fetch buffer:javaDeserializer.java
The default falls back to thebyte[]method,so existing deserializers are unaffected,andByteBufferDeserializeroverrides it to skip the copy.
The producer has no matching method.Serializeronly returnsbyte[]:
javaSerializer.java
So a producer whose record value is already in aByteBufferhas to copy it into abyte[]for everyrecord.This is the case for a caller that holds data off the Java heap or in a reused buffer,for examplea NettyByteBufexposed throughnioBuffer(),or a service that forwards a payload it does not read.
This KIP adds the missing method so the write side matches the read side that KIP-863 already added.It isopt-in, soa serializer that returnsbyte[]keeps working with no change.
Public Interfaces
Serializer.serializeToBuffer
A new default method onorg.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serializer<T>:
javaSerializer.java
A separate name is used because Java cannot overload on the return type alone.
ByteBufferSerializer
org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.ByteBufferSerializeroverrides the method to return the bufferwithout copying:
javaByteBufferSerializer.java
duplicate()gives the producer its own position and limit.The caller's buffer is left unchanged and canbe refilled and reused for the next record.
Partitioner.partitionwith a ByteBuffer key
A new default method onorg.apache.kafka.clients.producer.Partitioner,so that choosing the partitionfrom the key does not force abyte[]copy of the key:javaPartitioner.java
A customPartitionerthat implements only thebyte[]method keeps working.It receives a copied key,the same as today.Only the built-in partitioner skips the copy.
Proposed Changes
KafkaProducer.doSendcallsserializeToBufferin place ofserialize.For the default serializers thiswraps thebyte[]and behaves as before.ForByteBufferSerializerit passes the caller's buffer throughwith no copy.
The producer already copies the payload into the record batch once,when it writes the record.This only change removes the extra per-recordbyte[]that the serializer uses to allocate.The producerreads the returned buffer without moving its position,so a caller can hand in the sameByteBufferonevery send and refill it in place.
Currently,Utils#murmur2 hash operates on byte[]array and we would provide bit identical version backed bya ByteBuffer.
All references from MemoryRecordsBuilder->DefaultRecord operate on ByteBuffers.However,there is animplementation cost associated with the Utils#writeTo method that currently does a array copy directlysince the backing store for the ByteBuffer is a byte array.For uncompressed payloads,we can writethe ByteBufferDataOutputStream directly into the appendStream of MemoryRecordsBuilder.
Extension Considerations
This method is the serializer step of the send path.It removes the copy where the value enters theproducer.It does not by itself,keep the value off the heap all the way to the socket in the current flow.A caller who wants that should know the points where the value still touches the heap today.Each is a separate concern and is not part of this KIP.
